title: Smoothness over a product ring is checked factorwise
statement: Let $\varphi_1:R_1\to A_1$ and $\varphi_2:R_2\to A_2$ be homomorphisms of commutative rings, and make $A_1\times A_2$ an $R_1\times R_2$-algebra via $\varphi_1\times\varphi_2:(r_1,r_2)\mapsto(\varphi_1(r_1),\varphi_2(r_2))$. If $\varphi_1$ and $\varphi_2$ are smooth ring maps [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map], then $\varphi_1\times\varphi_2:R_1\times R_2\to A_1\times A_2$ is a smooth ring map.

source.place: No Stacks lemma states it in this form; Stacks uses it implicitly in Smoothing Ring Maps, Lemma Tag 07F3 (smoothing.tex line 1926). It follows from Algebra, Lemma Tag 0GIF (lemma-product-smooth, line 37613: a product S'xS'' of R-algebras is smooth over R iff both factors are) applied over R = R_1 x R_2, together with Lemma Tag 00TD (lemma-compose-smooth, line 37597) for R_1 x R_2 -> R_k -> A_k, where the projection R_1 x R_2 -> R_1 is the principal localization at the idempotent (1,0) (smooth, e.g. standard smooth R[x]/((1,0)x-1), Lemma Tag 00T7 lemma-standard-smooth)

proof.text: *Step 1 (the projections are smooth).* Put $R=R_1\times R_2$, $e_1=(1,0)$, and let $p_1:R\to R_1$, $(r_1,r_2)\mapsto r_1$, be the first projection, a surjective ring homomorphism making $R_1$ an $R$-algebra. We show that $R_1$ has a standard smooth presentation over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-standard-smooth-algebra] with $n=c=1$ and $f_1=f=e_1x-1\in R[x]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Writing a polynomial $P=\sum_k (a_k,b_k)x^k\in R[x]$ as the pair $(P_1,P_2)=(\sum_k a_kx^k,\sum_k b_kx^k)$ identifies $R[x]$ with the product ring $R_1[x]\times R_2[x]$ (sums and products of polynomials are computed from sums and products of coefficients, which are componentwise in $R$); under it $f=(x-1,-1)$. Let $\pi:R[x]\to R_1$, $P\mapsto P_1(1)$; it is a ring homomorphism (evaluation at $1$ after the first projection), it restricts to $p_1$ on $R$, so it is an $R$-algebra map, and it is surjective (the constant $(r_1,0)$ maps to $r_1$). Its kernel is $(f)$: $\pi(f)=1-1=0$; conversely if $P_1(1)=0$ then $P_1=(x-1)Q_1$ for some $Q_1\in R_1[x]$ (division by the monic $x-1$, remainder $P_1(1)=0$), and then $P=(P_1,P_2)=(x-1,-1)\cdot(Q_1,-P_2)=f\cdot(Q_1,-P_2)$. So $\pi$ induces an $R$-algebra isomorphism $\alpha:R[x]/(f)\xrightarrow{\sim}R_1$. The $1\times1$ Jacobian determinant is $g=\partial f/\partial x=e_1$, whose image in $R_1$ is $\pi(e_1)=p_1(e_1)=1$, a unit. Hence $p_1:R\to R_1$ is standard smooth, and smooth by [lem-weil-pbc-standard-smooth-is-smooth]. By symmetry (with $e_2=(0,1)$ and $f=e_2x-1$) the second projection $p_2:R\to R_2$ is smooth.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00T7 (lemma-standard-smooth, line 37274), part (1), applied to the presentation R_1 = R[x]/((1,0)x-1) of the item's source line; the kernel computation is written out by the agent

proof.text: *Step 2 (each factor is smooth over $R$).* Make $A_1$ an $R$-algebra by $\psi_1=\varphi_1\circ p_1:R\to R_1\to A_1$, $(r_1,r_2)\mapsto\varphi_1(r_1)$, and $A_2$ by $\psi_2=\varphi_2\circ p_2$. Since $p_1$ is smooth (Step 1) and $\varphi_1$ is smooth (hypothesis), the composite $\psi_1$ is smooth by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-base-change-composition] (2); likewise $\psi_2$ is smooth.

*Step 3 (the product).* By Step 2, $A_1$ and $A_2$ are smooth $R$-algebras via $\psi_1,\psi_2$, so by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-product-algebra] (with $S'=A_1$, $S''=A_2$) the product ring $A_1\times A_2$ is smooth over $R$ via $r\mapsto(\psi_1(r),\psi_2(r))$. For $r=(r_1,r_2)$ this is $(\varphi_1(r_1),\varphi_2(r_2))=(\varphi_1\times\varphi_2)(r)$, so the structure map of $A_1\times A_2$ over $R$ is exactly $\varphi_1\times\varphi_2$, which is therefore a smooth ring map [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map].
